Unalamation (pronounced: un-ala-mation) is non-inflammatory homeostatic physiology of the so called 'inflammatory' lipid mediators. 'Inflammatory' mediators maintain normal homeostatic physiological functions under the influence of anti-inflammatory lipid mediators. When there is injury, physical or microbial, acute inflammation is triggered by the biosynthesis of inflammatory lipid mediators such as prostaglandins and leukotrienes. Levels of these inflammatory mediators descend to normal tissue concentrations as the acute inflammation is resolved. In certain tissues such as kidneys, heart, brain, intestines, and during physiological changes such as ovulation and parturition, these 'inflammatory' lipid mediators are present at high concentrations or increased during the physiological change. Yet, there are no signs of inflammation. It is the simultaneous presence of anti-inflammatory lipid mediators such as epoxy polyunsaturated fatty acids that regulate the inflammatory propensity of prostaglandins towards homeostasis and this is designated as unalamation.

Beeliada, also known as Eliada, was a son of King David.
Name of Well
Beera was a leader of the tribe of Reuben, taken into exile by the Assyrians.
Beeraha was another name for Beera, a leader of the tribe of Reuben.
Beerelim is mentioned in Isaiah 15:8 as a location in Moab. The name means 'well of the mighty ones' and is associated with the cries of mourning that spread throughout Moab.
Father of Judith, Esau's wife, and also the father of Hosea
A town in the territory of one of the tribes of Israel.
Beeshterah is a city of refuge assigned to the Levites in the territory of Manasseh, east of the Jordan River, as mentioned in Joshua 21:27. It is also known as Ashtaroth.
A region or city associated with a key biblical figure.
Last king of Babylon, mentioned in the book of Daniel
King of Aram, opponent of Israel
Ben-hail was one of the officials sent by King Jehoshaphat to teach the law in the cities of Judah.
Commander of David's bodyguards, known for his bravery
Ben-ammi was the son of Lot and his younger daughter, and the ancestor of the Ammonites.
Beneberak is a town in the territory of Dan, mentioned in Joshua 19:45. It is located near the Philistine border and was part of the land allotted to the tribe of Dan.

Benejaakan is a place mentioned in the wilderness journeys of the Israelites, located in the territory of the Edomites (Numbers 33:31-32). It is named after the descendants of Jaakan, one of the Horite clans.
Benhanan was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogies.
Beninu was one of the leaders who signed the covenant with Nehemiah.
A place mentioned in the context of the division of the land.
Benzoheth was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogies.
Beon is mentioned in Numbers 32:3 as one of the cities in the land of Gilead that the tribe of Reuben requested to inhabit after the conquest of the Transjordan.
Father of Balaam, mentioned in Numbers
Name means 'blessing,' associated with a valley in Chronicles
Berachiah was the father of Asaph, a prominent Levite musician.
Beraiah was a descendant of Ephraim, mentioned in the genealogies.
Father of Zechariah, a prophet
Bered is a place mentioned in Genesis 16:14, located near the well where Hagar encountered the angel of the Lord. It is also the name of a descendant of Ephraim (1 Chronicles 7:20).
Son of Asher, founder of a clan in Israel
A city or region involved in a significant biblical event.
A location in the wilderness journey of the Israelites.
The god of the covenant at Shechem, whose house the men of the tower of Shechem entered in the days of Abimelech.
Berodach-baladan was a king of Babylon who sent envoys to Hezekiah after his recovery from illness.

Berothah is a city mentioned in Ezekiel 47:16 as part of the northern boundary of the land allotted to Israel. It is identified with the region of Berothai, which was associated with the kingdom of Zobah.
Berothai is a city mentioned in 2 Samuel 8:8, which was captured by King David during his campaign against Hadadezer, king of Zobah. The city is also referred to as 'Berothah' in Ezekiel 47:16.
A person or place mentioned in the genealogies or lists.
Ancestor of a family of temple servants
Besodeiah was the father of Meshullam, who helped repair the wall of Jerusalem.

The Brook Besor is mentioned in 1 Samuel 30:9-21 as the place where David's men rested while pursuing the Amalekites. Those who stayed behind at the brook to rest were later rewarded equally with those who fought.
Betah is a city captured by King David from Hadadezer, king of Zobah, as mentioned in 2 Samuel 8:8. The city's wealth in bronze was taken by David and later used for the temple's construction.
Beten is a town in the territory of the tribe of Asher, mentioned in Joshua 19:25. It was part of the land allotted to Asher during the division of Canaan.

Beth-baal-meon is a town in the territory of Reuben, east of the Jordan River. It is mentioned in Joshua 13:17 and was later known simply as Baalmeon. It was associated with the worship of the god Baal.
Beth-ezel was a town in Judah mentioned in the book of Micah.
Beth-gader was a town in the territory of Judah, mentioned in the genealogies.
A location described in the context of Israel's geography.
Beth-rapha was a descendant of Judah, mentioned in the genealogies.
A town mentioned in the book of Joshua or Chronicles.
Beth-zur is a town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:58. It was fortified by Rehoboam and played a significant role in the Maccabean Revolt.
Bethanath is a town in the territory of the tribe of Naphtali, mentioned in Joshua 19:38. It was one of the towns whose inhabitants were not driven out by the Israelites.
Bethanoth is a town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:59. It was part of the land allotted to the tribe of Judah during the division of Canaan.
Betharabah is a city on the border of the tribes of Judah and Benjamin, mentioned in Joshua 15:6 and Joshua 18:22. It is located near the Jordan River and the Dead Sea, within the desert region.
Betharam is a city east of the Jordan River, mentioned in Joshua 13:27 as part of the inheritance of the tribe of Gad. It was later fortified by Herod the Great and renamed Julias.

Betharbel is mentioned in Hosea 10:14 as a site of a devastating battle where the people were slaughtered. The exact location of Betharbel is uncertain, but it is used as a symbol of destruction and judgment.
Bethaven is a name that means 'house of wickedness' and is used in the Bible to describe Bethel after it became a center of idol worship. It is mentioned in Joshua 7:2 and 1 Samuel 13:5.
Bethazmaveth is a village mentioned in Nehemiah 7:28 as one of the places where the people of Judah lived after returning from the Babylonian exile. It was located near Jerusalem.
Bethbarah is a place mentioned in Judges 7:24, where the Ephraimites captured the Midianites as they fled from Gideon. It is located near the Jordan River, and its name means 'house of the ford.'
Bethbirei is a town in the territory of Simeon, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:31. It was one of the cities given to the tribe of Simeon within the larger territory of Judah.
Bethcar is mentioned in 1 Samuel 7:11 as the place to which the Israelites pursued the Philistines after their victory at Mizpah. The name means 'house of the lamb.'

Bethdagon is the name of two towns mentioned in the Bible: one in the territory of Judah (Joshua 15:41) and one in the territory of Asher (Joshua 19:27). Both towns were likely centers of worship for the Philistine god Dagon.
Bethdiblathaim is a Moabite city mentioned in Jeremiah 48:22 as one of the cities facing judgment from God. It is thought to be the same as Almon-Diblathaim mentioned in Numbers 33:46.
A city linked to the historical or prophetic books of the Bible.
Bethemek is a town in the territory of the tribe of Asher, mentioned in Joshua 19:27. Its name means 'house of the valley,' indicating its likely location in a lowland area.
Bether is mentioned in Song of Solomon 2:17 as a location associated with the mountains. The term 'mountains of Bether' is often interpreted symbolically in the context of the Song of Solomon.
Bethgamul is a town in Moab mentioned in Jeremiah 48:23 as one of the cities facing judgment. The name means 'house of recompense' and it was likely a significant location in Moabite territory.

Bethhaccerem, meaning 'house of the vineyard,' is mentioned in Nehemiah 3:14 and Jeremiah 6:1. It was a district in Judah and served as a signal station where a fire beacon was lit to warn of approaching danger.
Bethharan is a city east of the Jordan River, mentioned in Numbers 32:36 as part of the territory given to the tribe of Gad. It was later fortified and renamed 'Betharam' by Herod the Great.

Bethhogla is a town in the territory of Benjamin, mentioned in Joshua 15:6 and Joshua 18:19-21. It is located near the Jordan River and the Dead Sea, marking the boundary between the tribes of Judah and Benjamin.

Bethhoglah, also spelled Bethhogla, is a town in the territory of Benjamin, located near the Jordan River and the Dead Sea. It is mentioned in Joshua 18:19-21 as part of the boundary descriptions of the tribal allotments.

Bethhoron consists of two towns, Upper Bethhoron and Lower Bethhoron, in the territory of Ephraim. They are mentioned in several passages, including Joshua 10:10-11, as the site of battles and were strategically important due to their location on a major ascent.

Bethjeshimoth is a town located east of the Jordan River, mentioned in Joshua 12:3 and Joshua 13:20. It was part of the territory assigned to the tribe of Reuben and was located near the plains of Moab.
Bethjesimoth is another spelling of Bethjeshimoth, a town located east of the Jordan River in the territory of Reuben. It was situated near the plains of Moab and mentioned in Numbers 33:49.
Bethlebaoth is a town in the southern part of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 19:6. It was part of the inheritance given to the tribe of Simeon.

Bethlehemjudah is another name for Bethlehem, emphasizing its location within the tribe of Judah. It is mentioned in the context of various biblical stories, including the story of Ruth and the birthplace of Jesus.
Bethmaachah is a city in northern Israel mentioned in 2 Samuel 20:14-15. It was besieged by Joab during the rebellion of Sheba, son of Bichri.
Bethmarcaboth is a town in the territory of Simeon, mentioned in Joshua 19:5 and 1 Chronicles 4:31. The name means 'house of chariots,' indicating its possible use as a chariot station.
Bethmeon is another name for Bethbaalmeon, a town in the territory of Reuben, east of the Jordan River. It is mentioned in Jeremiah 48:23 as part of the Moabite territory facing judgment.
Bethnimrah is a city in the territory of Gad, east of the Jordan River, mentioned in Numbers 32:36 and Joshua 13:27. It was fortified by the tribe of Gad and is located near the plains of Moab.
Bethpalet is a town in the southern part of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:27. It was part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah after the conquest of Canaan.

Bethpeor is a location east of the Jordan River, associated with the worship of the Moabite god Baal-peor. It is mentioned in Deuteronomy 3:29 and Deuteronomy 4:46 as a place where Moses delivered his final speeches.
Bethphelet is a town mentioned in Nehemiah 11:26 as part of the places where the people of Judah lived after the return from exile. It is likely located in the southern part of Judah.

Bethrehob is a town in the territory of the tribe of Naphtali, mentioned in Judges 18:28 and 2 Samuel 10:6. It is located near the city of Dan and was involved in the events surrounding the tribe of Dan's migration.

Bethshan, also known as Bethshean, is a significant city in the Jordan Valley mentioned in 1 Samuel 31:10 and 2 Samuel 21:12. It is where the bodies of Saul and his sons were hung on the city wall by the Philistines after their defeat at Mount Gilboa.

Bethshean, also spelled Bethshan, is a city in the Jordan Valley known for its role in the story of King Saul's defeat by the Philistines. It was later a major administrative center during the reign of King Solomon (1 Kings 4:12).

Bethshemesh is a Levitical city in the territory of Judah, mentioned in several passages including Joshua 15:10. It is the place where the Ark of the Covenant was returned by the Philistines after it caused plagues in their cities (1 Samuel 6:12-15).

Bethshittah is mentioned in Judges 7:22 as the place where the Midianites fled during Gideon's surprise attack. The name means 'house of the acacia' and indicates the presence of acacia trees in the area.
Bethtappuah is a town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:53. The name means 'house of apples,' suggesting it was an area known for apple orchards.
Bethul is a town in the territory of Simeon, mentioned in Joshua 19:4. It was part of the inheritance given to Simeon within the land of Judah.
Betonim is a town in the territory of Gad, mentioned in Joshua 13:26. It is located in the region east of the Jordan River, within the land allotted to the tribe of Gad.
Ancestor of a family of returnees from Babylon.
Craftsman filled with the Spirit of God to construct the Tabernacle.
Bezek is a town mentioned in Judges 1:4-5, where the Israelites defeated the Canaanites and Perizzites. It is also where Saul mustered the Israelites to fight against the Ammonites (1 Samuel 11:8).

Bezer is a city of refuge located in the wilderness on the plateau east of the Jordan, mentioned in Deuteronomy 4:43 and Joshua 20:8. It was designated as a refuge for those who accidentally committed manslaughter.
Father of Sheba, who led a rebellion against King David.
Bidkar was the chariot officer of Jehu, who helped execute King Joram.
Bigtha was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus of Persia.
Bigthan was one of the eunuchs of King Ahasuerus who conspired against him.
Bigthana was one of the eunuchs who conspired against King Ahasuerus.
Leader of a group of returnees from Babylon.
One of Job's friends who argued with him during his trials.
Bileam is a town in the territory of Manasseh, mentioned in 1 Chronicles 6:70. It was given to the Levites as part of their inheritance.
Priestly family mentioned in Chronicles and Nehemiah.
Bilgai was a priest who signed the covenant with Nehemiah.
Descendant of Esau, mentioned in Genesis and Chronicles.
One of the returnees from Babylon.
Bimhal was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogies.
Descendant of Saul, mentioned in Chronicles.
Ancestor of a family of returnees from Babylon.
Birsha was the king of Gomorrah who fought in the battle of the Vale of Siddim.
Birzavith was a descendant of Asher, mentioned in the genealogies.
Bishlam was one of the officials who wrote to Artaxerxes against the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
Bithiah was the daughter of Pharaoh who married Mered, a descendant of Judah.
Bithron is a region east of the Jordan River mentioned in 2 Samuel 2:29. It is the area through which Abner and his men retreated after a battle with Joab's forces.
Bithynia is a Roman province in Asia Minor, mentioned in Acts 16:7 and 1 Peter 1:1. Paul was prevented by the Holy Spirit from preaching there during his missionary journeys.
Bizjothjah is a town in the southern part of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:28. It was part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah.
Biztha was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus (Xerxes) of Persia. He is mentioned in the Book of Esther as one of the officials who attended the king during his banquets.
Blastus was the chamberlain of King Herod Agrippa I, who facilitated negotiations between Herod and the people of Tyre and Sidon.
Son of Jeconiah, mentioned in Chronicles.
Bochim, meaning 'weepers,' is the name given to the place where the Israelites wept after an angel of the Lord rebuked them for failing to drive out the inhabitants of the land (Judges 2:1-5).
Boscath is a town in Judah mentioned in 2 Kings 22:1 as the birthplace of King Josiah's mother, Jedidah.

Bosor is the Greek form of Beor, the father of Balaam, the prophet who was hired by Balak to curse Israel. Bosor is mentioned in 2 Peter 2:15 in the New Testament, referring to Balaam's corrupt actions.
Bozez is one of the two rocky crags mentioned in 1 Samuel 14:4 that Jonathan and his armor-bearer climbed to attack the Philistine outpost.
Bozkath is a town in Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:39. It was near Lachish and is notable for being the home of King Josiah's mother, Jedidah.
High priest during the time of the Judges.
Levite musician during King David's reign.
Name of Month
Bunah was one of the sons of Jerahmeel, a descendant of Judah, listed in the genealogies in the Book of 1 Chronicles.
Ancestor of a family of Levites, mentioned in Nehemiah.
Descendant of Nahor, mentioned in Genesis.
Buzi was the father of the prophet Ezekiel.
A man of Buz; Elihu the Buzite, who answered Job, was of the kindred of Ram.
Cabbon is a town in the territory of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:40. It was part of the southern hill country of Judah.
Cabul is a town in the territory of Asher, mentioned in Joshua 19:27. It is also the name of a district given by Solomon to Hiram, king of Tyre, which Hiram found unsatisfactory (1 Kings 9:13).
Cainan is mentioned in Genesis 5:9-14 as a descendant of Adam through Seth. He lived 910 years and was the father of Mahalalel.
Calcol was a wise man, a descendant of Zerah, whose wisdom was surpassed only by Solomon.
Calebephratah is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 2:24 as the place where Hezron died. It is associated with Caleb, one of the leaders of Israel.
Calno is a city mentioned in Isaiah 10:9, often identified with Calneh. It was one of the cities conquered by the Assyrian king, and its fate was used as a warning to Israel.
Camon is the place where the judge Jair was buried, as mentioned in Judges 10:5. It is believed to be located in Gilead, east of the Jordan River.
The inhabitants of Canaan before Israel, descendants of Canaan, whom Israel was commanded to dispossess.
Canneh is mentioned in the Book of Ezekiel as one of the cities or trading centers associated with the city of Tyre. It was likely located in Mesopotamia, near Babylon.
The Caphthorim were descendants of Mizraim, considered to be one of the early groups of people who lived in Caphtor, often identified with Crete or regions in the eastern Mediterranean.
Similar to Caphthorim, they are descendants of Mizraim and are traditionally associated with the region of Caphtor. They are sometimes linked to the Philistines in later texts.
A place in the territory of one of the Israelite tribes.
Carcas was one of the seven eunuchs who served King Ahasuerus.

Carchemish is a significant ancient city on the Euphrates River, mentioned in Isaiah 10:9 and Jeremiah 46:2. It was the site of a major battle between the Babylonians and the Egyptians, which led to the decline of Egyptian power in the region.
Careah was the father of Johanan, who was a leader among the remnant of Judah left after the Babylonian conquest.
A location associated with prophetic visions or events.
Carshena was one of the seven princes of Persia who advised King Ahasuerus.
Casiphia is a place mentioned in Ezra 8:17, where Ezra sent for Levites to join the group returning to Jerusalem from Babylon. It is thought to be located near the Euphrates River.
A station during the Israelites' wilderness journey.
The sign of the Alexandrian ship that carried Paul from Melita toward Rome, named for the twin sons of Zeus in Greek myth.

Cedron, also known as the Kidron Valley, is a valley on the eastern side of Jerusalem mentioned in John 18:1. It is the place where Jesus crossed on his way to the Garden of Gethsemane before his arrest.
Cenchrea is a port town near Corinth, mentioned in Acts 18:18 and Romans 16:1. It was one of the places from which Paul set sail during his missionary journeys.
Chalcol was a wise man, a descendant of Zerah, whose wisdom was surpassed only by Solomon.
A person or family listed among those who returned from exile.
Chaldea, also known as Babylonia, was a region in southern Mesopotamia. It was home to the Chaldeans, who ruled Babylon and were known for their wisdom and astrology (Jeremiah 50:10).
A border or boundary described in the context of Israel's land.
A place mentioned in a prophecy or historical narrative.
Chanaan is an alternative spelling of Canaan, the land promised to the descendants of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. It is mentioned in Acts 7:11 and Acts 13:19 in the New Testament.
Charashim, meaning 'craftsmen,' is a place mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:14. It is associated with families skilled in various crafts and trades.

Charchemish is an alternative spelling of Carchemish, a significant ancient city on the Euphrates River, mentioned in 2 Chronicles 35:20. It was the site of a major battle between the Babylonians and Egyptians.

Charran is another name for Haran, the city where Abraham's father Terah settled and died. It is mentioned in Acts 7:2-4 as the place where God called Abraham to leave his family and go to the Promised Land.
Chebar is a river in Babylonia, mentioned in the book of Ezekiel. It is where Ezekiel received his visions and prophecies during the Babylonian exile (Ezekiel 1:1-3).
King of Elam, led an alliance of kings against Sodom and Gomorrah.
Chelal was one of those who had married foreign wives and was required to send them away during Ezra's reforms.
Chelluh was another person who had married foreign wives and was required to send them away.
Descendant of Caleb, mentioned in Chronicles.
Chelubai is an alternative name for Caleb, one of the Israelite spies sent into Canaan. He was a leader from the tribe of Judah.
A town in the territory of one of the tribes of Israel.
Father of Zedekiah, a false prophet, mentioned in Kings and Chronicles.
Chenani was one of the Levites who stood on the stairs and cried out to the Lord during the public confession of sins by the Israelites.
Chief of the Levites in charge of the music during David's reign.
Chepharhaammonai is a town in the territory of Benjamin, mentioned in Joshua 18:24. Its name means 'village of the Ammonites,' indicating its possible origin or inhabitants.
Chephirah is one of the cities of the Gibeonites, mentioned in Joshua 9:17 and Joshua 18:26. It was part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Benjamin.
Descendant of Seir, mentioned in Genesis.
A region or city associated with a key biblical figure.
A location linked with the exodus or conquest narratives.
The Brook Cherith is the place where the prophet Elijah hid and was fed by ravens during a time of drought, as mentioned in 1 Kings 17:3-5.
Chesalon is a town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:10. It is located near the western boundary of Judah's territory.
Chesil is a town in the southern part of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:30. It was part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah.
Chesulloth is a town in the territory of Issachar, mentioned in Joshua 19:18. It was located near the border of the tribe's land and was one of the cities within Issachar's inheritance.
Chezib is a town in the territory of Judah, mentioned in Genesis 38:5. It is the place where Judah's wife gave birth to his son, Shelah.
The threshing floor of Chidon is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 13:9 as the place where Uzzah touched the Ark of the Covenant and was struck down by God.
Chileab was the second son of David, born to him by Abigail. He is also known as Daniel in some references.
Son of Naomi, husband of Orpah, mentioned in the Book of Ruth.
Chilmad is a place mentioned in Ezekiel 27:23 as one of the trading partners of Tyre. It is associated with a region known for its commerce and trade in ancient times.
Follower of David, mentioned in Samuel and Jeremiah.

Chinnereth, also known as Kinnereth, is a town and a region near the Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Chinnereth. It is mentioned in Numbers 34:11 and Deuteronomy 3:17 as part of the Promised Land's boundaries.

Chinneroth, also spelled Kinneroth, is a fortified town in the territory of Naphtali, mentioned in Joshua 11:2 and Joshua 19:35. It is located near the Sea of Galilee, also called the Sea of Chinneroth.
Name of Month
Chislon was the father of Elidad, who was a leader of the tribe of Benjamin during the distribution of the Promised Land.
Chislothtabor is a town on the border of the territory of Zebulun, mentioned in Joshua 19:12. It is located near Mount Tabor in the region of Galilee.
A pagan star-god named in Amos, whom Israel is charged with bearing in the wilderness alongside Moloch.
Chorashan is a town mentioned in 1 Samuel 30:30 as one of the places where David sent spoils after his victory over the Amalekites. It is located in the southern part of Judah.
A town of Galilee which Jesus upbraided with Bethsaida, because it saw his mighty works and did not repent.
Chozeba is mentioned in 1 Chronicles 4:22 as the ancestral home of the descendants of Shelah, a son of Judah. It is also known as Chezib or Achzib.
A city or region involved in a significant biblical event.
King of Mesopotamia, first oppressor of Israel after Joshua's death.
Chuza was the steward of Herod Antipas, and his wife Joanna was one of the women who followed and supported Jesus.
Cilicia is a region in southeastern Asia Minor (modern-day Turkey), mentioned in Acts 6:9 and other passages. It was the home region of the Apostle Paul (Acts 21:39).
Cinneroth, also known as Kinneroth, is a fortified town in the territory of Naphtali, mentioned in Joshua 19:35. It is located near the Sea of Galilee, which is also called the Sea of Chinneroth.
Clauda is a small island mentioned in Acts 27:16, where Paul and his companions passed by during a storm on their way to Rome. It is located south of Crete in the Mediterranean Sea.
Cleophas is traditionally understood to be the same person as Cleopas, though some consider them distinct. He was possibly the husband of one of the Marys at the crucifixion of Jesus.
Cnidus is a city on the southwestern coast of Asia Minor, mentioned in Acts 27:7. Paul's ship struggled to pass by Cnidus due to unfavorable winds during his voyage to Rome.
Ancestor of a family of returnees, mentioned in Nehemiah.
Colosse is a city in the region of Phrygia in Asia Minor, mentioned in Colossians 1:2. It is the recipient of Paul's letter to the Colossians.
Conaniah was a Levite during the reign of Josiah, who helped distribute the offerings for the temple service.
Another name for Jehoiachin, king of Judah.
Levite, overseer of the offerings, mentioned in Chronicles.
Cosam is listed in the genealogy of Jesus in the Gospel of Luke, though little else is known about him.
A messianic title of the promised child in Isaiah, spelled Counseller in the KJV: Wonderful, Counseller, The mighty God.
Midianite woman killed by Phinehas for leading Israel into idolatry.
Crescens is mentioned in 2 Timothy 4:10 as one of Paul's companions who went to Galatia. Not much else is known about him.
A person or place mentioned in the genealogies or lists.
A location described in the context of Israel's geography.
Cushan is a region or people mentioned in Habakkuk 3:7. It is often identified with Cush, the region south of Egypt, or with the Midianites.
Father of Zephaniah, mentioned in Kings and Chronicles.
Cuth is mentioned in 2 Kings 17:30 as one of the regions from which the Assyrians brought people to resettle Samaria. The people of Cuth worshiped the god Nergal.
Cuthah is a city in Babylonia mentioned in 2 Kings 17:24. The Assyrians brought people from Cuthah to repopulate the land of Israel after the Northern Kingdom was exiled.
A town mentioned in the book of Joshua or Chronicles.
Cyrenius, also known as Quirinius, was a Roman governor of Syria who conducted a census mentioned in the Gospel of Luke.
Dabareh is a Levitical city in the territory of Issachar, mentioned in Joshua 21:28. It is located near Mount Tabor.
Dabbasheth is a town in the territory of Zebulun, mentioned in Joshua 19:11. It was part of the land allotted to the tribe of Zebulun.
Daberath is a town on the border of the tribes of Issachar and Zebulun, mentioned in Joshua 19:12 and 1 Chronicles 6:72. It was a Levitical city given to the Gershonite Levites.
Dalaiah was one of the descendants of David listed in the genealogies in Chronicles.
Dalmanutha is a place on the western shore of the Sea of Galilee, mentioned in Mark 8:10. Jesus went there after feeding the 4,000, but its exact location remains uncertain.
Dalphon was one of the ten sons of Haman who were killed by the Jews in the Book of Esther.
A city linked to the historical or prophetic books of the Bible.
Danjaan is a town mentioned in 2 Samuel 24:6 as part of the northernmost extent of King David's census. Its exact location is not definitively known.
Dannah is a town in the hill country of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:49. It was part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah.
Rebelled against Moses, mentioned in Exodus and Numbers.
A Canaanite king defeated by Joshua, also refers to a town in Judah.
Descendant of Abraham, associated with a region in Arabia.
Dedanim refers to the descendants of Dedan, a son of Raamah, mentioned in Isaiah 21:13. They were a trading people living in northern Arabia, known for their caravans.
A tribe or location mentioned in biblical context.
Dekar was one of Solomon's twelve district governors, responsible for providing food supplies for the king and his household.
Priestly family, mentioned in Chronicles and Nehemiah.
Derbe is a city in the region of Lycaonia, mentioned in Acts 14:6, Acts 16:1, and Acts 20:4. Paul visited Derbe during his missionary journeys, and it was the hometown of his companion, Gaius.
Diblaim was the father of Gomer, the wife of the prophet Hosea, mentioned in the Book of Hosea.
Diblath is a place mentioned in Ezekiel 6:14 as a location where God would bring judgment upon Israel. It is often identified with the region of Riblah in northern Syria.
Dibon is a city in Moab, mentioned in Numbers 21:30 and Numbers 32:3. It was rebuilt by the tribe of Gad and later became an important Moabite city.
Dibongad is a place mentioned in Numbers 33:45-46 as one of the encampments of the Israelites during their wilderness journey. It is closely associated with Dibon in Moab.
Dibri was a member of the tribe of Dan, whose daughter was involved in an incident where a man blasphemed God and was stoned according to the law in Leviticus.
Another name for Thomas, one of the twelve apostles.
Descendant of Joktan, mentioned in Genesis and Chronicles.
Dilean is a town in the lowlands of Judah, mentioned in Joshua 15:38. It was part of the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah.
Dimnah is a Levitical city in the territory of Zebulun, mentioned in Joshua 21:35. It was one of the cities given to the Levites.
A city in the territory of Judah, mentioned among the towns in the southern part of the tribe's allotment (Joshua 15:22).
A people named among those settled in Samaria who wrote to Artaxerxes against the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
A city in Edom, known as the royal city of Bela, one of the kings of Edom before Israel had kings (Genesis 36:32; 1 Chronicles 1:43).
